kaps_punt: Vaste stowwe, vloeistowwe en gasse: vaste stowwe, vloeistowwe en gasse maak al die materiaal rondom ons uit; 'n paar eienskappe van vastestowwe, vloeistowwe en gasse -- vastestowwe behou hul vorm -- vloeistowwe vloei en neem die vorm van die houer aan -- gasse, soos lug, is geneig om te versprei, het geen definitiewe vorm nie maar kan saamgevat word (soos in 'n ballon)

items.bewering: Elke voorwerp wat jy om jou sien, is van een of ander materiaal gemaak.
items.blok: Alles om jou is van materiaal gemaak
items.bron: Wikipedia, 'Material': 'A material is a substance or mixture of substances that constitutes an object.' Universal quantifier 'elke' tested literally: holds, because by definition every object is made of some material.

items.bewering: Baie stoele is van hout gemaak, en baie bottels is van plastiek. Die bottel self is die voorwerp, en plastiek is sy materiaal.
items.blok: Alles om jou is van materiaal gemaak
items.bron: Wikipedia, 'Material': plastics are materials, illustrated with a plastic water bottle; the object/material distinction follows from the definition ('constitutes an object'). 'Baie' (many), not 'all', so the quantifier holds.

items.bewering: Die water binne die bottel is ook 'n materiaal. Die lug wat jy nou inasem, is ook materiaal, al sien jy dit nie.
items.blok: Alles om jou is van materiaal gemaak
items.bron: University of Illinois Physics Van, 'Does air take up space?' (van.physics.illinois.edu/ask/listing/3157): air spreads through a space and occupies it; blowing up and squeezing a balloon shows something is inside. The lesson's own CAPS bullet counts gases such as air among the materials around us. Air is invisible: standard.

items.bewering: Vaste stowwe, vloeistowwe en gasse is drie soorte materiaal. Hierdie drie maak saam al die materiaal om jou uit.
items.blok: Alles om jou is van materiaal gemaak
items.bron: Wikipedia, 'State of matter': solid, liquid and gas are the classic states; plasma, the fourth everyday state, is 'not freely existing under normal conditions on Earth' (lightning, neon signs). The lesson repeats the CAPS bullet's own statement. 'al die materiaal' tested literally: holds at Grade 4 level; mixtures such as foam or mud are combinations of these states, and a child is not led to a false conclusion.

items.bewering: 'n Vaste stof het sy eie vorm, en dit hou daardie vorm. Tel 'n klip op en draai hom om. Sy vorm bly dieselfde.
items.blok: 'n Vaste stof hou sy eie vorm
items.bron: Wikipedia, 'State of matter': a solid has 'a stable, definite shape, and a definite volume'. Matches the CAPS bullet 'vastestowwe behou hul vorm'. Flexible solids (cloth) are handled explicitly elsewhere in the lesson, see the lap item.

items.bewering: Sit die klip in 'n glas en sit hom daarna in 'n bak. Hy neem nie die houer se vorm aan nie, en hy bly dieselfde klip.
items.blok: 'n Vaste stof hou sy eie vorm
items.bron: Wikipedia, 'State of matter' (solids keep a definite shape; it is liquids that adapt to the container). Activity tested literally: a stone placed in a glass and then a bowl keeps its shape.

items.bewering: Die vorm van 'n vaste stof kan wel verander as jy self iets daaraan doen. Jy kan 'n stok breek of 'n stuk klei platdruk. Dan het die ding 'n nuwe vorm, en hy hou daardie nuwe vorm ook.
items.blok: 'n Vaste stof hou sy eie vorm
items.bron: NSTA, 'Is It Solid?' (nsta.org/lesson-plan/it-solid): a solid's shape can be changed (dough, clay and other non-rigid solids remain solids). 'kan wel verander as' is not 'only if', so it does not exclude other causes. A broken stick and flattened clay keep the new shape: tested literally, holds.

items.bewering: 'n Vloeistof vloei, en jy kan dit van die een houer na die ander giet.
items.blok: 'n Vloeistof neem die houer se vorm aan
items.bron: Wikipedia, 'State of matter': liquid particles can slide past one another, so it flows; 'maintain a fixed volume while adapting to the shape of its container'.

items.bewering: Sit 'n klein hoeveelheid water in 'n bottel. Die water lê onder in die bottel, en dit is rond soos die bottel. Giet daardie water in 'n hoë, smal glas, en dit staan smal en hoog. Giet dit nou in 'n vlak bak, en dit lê breed en vlak.
items.blok: 'n Vloeistof neem die houer se vorm aan
items.bron: Wikipedia, 'State of matter' (liquid adapts to the shape of its container) and Wikipedia, 'Free surface' (the liquid settles at the bottom under gravity with a level top). Activity tested literally: holds; 'smal en hoog' is relative to the shallow bowl and true as a comparison. The comparison 'rond soos die bottel' maps correctly (the shape comes from the container).

items.bewering: Dit is elke keer dieselfde hoeveelheid water, en net die vorm verander.
items.blok: 'n Vloeistof neem die houer se vorm aan
items.bron: Wikipedia, 'State of matter': a liquid has a fixed volume while its shape changes with the container. A few drops left behind in the bottle do not make this misleading.

items.bewering: Water wat in 'n oop houer stilstaan, lê met sy boonste kant plat.
items.blok: 'n Vloeistof neem die houer se vorm aan
items.bron: Wikipedia, 'Free surface': 'on the surface of the Earth, all free surfaces of liquids are horizontal unless disturbed'. The only deviation is the meniscus at the wall, which is negligible at Grade 4. The condition 'stilstaan' is stated correctly.

items.bewering: Die houer bepaal dus 'n vloeistof se vorm en nie die vloeistof self nie.
items.blok: 'n Vloeistof neem die houer se vorm aan
items.bron: Wikipedia, 'State of matter' (liquid has no shape of its own and takes its container's shape). The level top is set by gravity rather than the container, but the sentence is about shape in general and holds at Grade 4 level.

items.bewering: 'n Gas het geen eie vorm nie, en dit bly nie op een plek nie. Dit versprei maklik, en dit vul die hele houer waarin dit is.
items.blok: 'n Gas versprei en het geen eie vorm nie
items.bron: Wikipedia, 'State of matter': a gas has no definite shape or volume and will 'expand to fill the container'. Illinois Physics Van: 'the air spreads around in the space'.

items.bewering: Jy kan 'n gas wel in 'n houer vaskeer en dit so bymekaar hou. Blaas 'n ballon op en knoop sy nek styf toe. Die knoop keer dat die lug by die nek uitkom.
items.blok: 'n Gas versprei en het geen eie vorm nie
items.bron: Illinois Physics Van ('you could blow up a balloon and see that the air you put inside it made it expand'); the CAPS bullet in the lesson ('kan saamgevat word (soos in 'n ballon)'). Activity tested literally: a knotted balloon holds its air (slow leakage through the rubber over hours is irrelevant here).

items.bewering: Die lug versprei binne die ballon en vul hom van onder tot bo. Die ronde vorm kom van die ballon self en nie van die lug nie.
items.blok: 'n Gas versprei en het geen eie vorm nie
items.bron: Wikipedia, 'State of matter' (a gas has no shape of its own and fills its container). Mapping tested: the same air in a long balloon takes a long shape, so the shape does come from the container. The air's pressure inflates the balloon, but the sentence is about where the SHAPE comes from, and on that it holds.

items.bewering: Lug is 'n gas, en jy kan dit nie sien nie. Dit is nogtans regte materiaal, en 'n opgeblase ballon wys dit.
items.blok: Lug is regte materiaal
items.bron: Illinois Physics Van, 'Does air take up space?': 'if you blow up a balloon and squeeze it you can feel that there is something inside it.' Air is a mixture of gases; calling it 'n gas' is the CAPS bullet's own wording ('gasse, soos lug').

items.bewering: Druk die ballon wat jy pas opgeblaas het, tussen jou twee hande. Jy kan hom 'n ent platdruk, maar hy spring terug sodra jy hom los. Iets binne die ballon stoot terug teen jou twee hande. Daardie iets is die lug wat jy self daarin geblaas het.
items.blok: Lug is regte materiaal
items.bron: Illinois Physics Van (squeezing an inflated balloon you feel something inside); same principle as the sealed bicycle pump and syringe there: trapped air resists being squeezed. Activity tested literally: holds. Saying the air does the pushing is the right mechanism, since an empty balloon squeezed the same way does not push back.

items.bewering: Vat 'n oop bottel wat leeg lyk en draai sy mond na onder. Druk die bottel se mond diep onder die water in 'n emmer in. Draai hom nou skuins, en groot borrels kom by die mond uit.
items.blok: Borrels uit 'n bottel
items.bron: MEL Science, 'Waterproof secret' and Colorado State University Little Shop of Physics, 'Flash Science: Surface Tension and Pressure' (lsop.colostate.edu): an inverted vessel pushed into water keeps its trapped air, and when it is tipped the air comes out as bubbles that rise to the surface. Activity tested step by step: works with an ordinary open bottle in a bucket.

items.bewering: Daardie borrels is die lug wat eers binne die bottel was. Die water styg by die mond in en neem die lug se plek in. Die bottel was dus nie leeg nie, maar vol lug.
items.blok: Borrels uit 'n bottel
items.bron: MEL Science, 'Waterproof secret': 'bubbles go up to the surface, and water eventually takes the place of the air'; the same activity concludes the glass was 'filled' with air. Colorado State LSOP describes the trapped air bubble in the inverted glass. 'styg ... in' is correct because the mouth points down.

items.bewering: Hout, klip en plastiek is vaste stowwe wat hul eie vorm hou.
items.blok: Voorbeelde van die drie soorte
items.bron: NSTA, 'Is It Solid?': wood and rock are listed among solids; Wikipedia, 'Material' (plastics are solid materials made into bottles and bowls). Thin plastic such as a bag is floppy, but it is still a solid, and the lesson's lap item covers flexible solids.

items.bewering: 'n Lap buig maklik, maar jy kan hom nie giet nie, en hy bly 'n vaste stof.
items.blok: Voorbeelde van die drie soorte
items.bron: NSTA, 'Is It Solid?': cloth is among the expected answers for solids, and children commonly place non-rigid materials 'in between a solid and liquid'. The sentence correctly counters that misconception.

items.bewering: Water, tee en vrugtesap is vloeistowwe wat 'n houer se vorm aanneem.
items.blok: Voorbeelde van die drie soorte
items.bron: Wikipedia, 'State of matter' (liquids take the shape of their container). Tea and fruit juice are water-based liquids.

items.bewering: Die kookolie in 'n pan is ook 'n vloeistof.

items.bron: Wikipedia, 'Cooking oil': 'Cooking oil is typically a liquid at room temperature' (exceptions such as coconut and palm oil are solid when cold but melt in a hot pan, so 'in 'n pan' holds even for those).

items.bron: Illinois Physics Van: 'If there's some space around (a box or a room) and there's air in it, the air spreads around in the space.'

items.blok: Voorbeelde van die drie soorte
items.bron: Sievert, LPG FAQ (sievert.se/en/faq/liquefied-petroleum-gas): LPG is stored as a liquid under pressure and 'when you open the valve ... liquid LPG rapidly evaporates into gas'. Afrox (South Africa) Handigas brochure: stored as a liquid under pressure in the cylinder; the stove burns the vapour. The sentence is about the gas burning at the stove, not the contents of the cylinder, so it is true. The comparison 'net soos lug' only maps the state, and that mapping holds.

items.bewering: Jy kan baie materiaal met drie vrae sorteer. Vra eers of jy dit kan giet. Vra dan of elke stuk heel bly wanneer niks dit vashou nie. Vra laastens of sy stil boonste kant plat lê.
items.blok: Hoe jy die drie uitmekaar ken
items.bron: Tested as a set against every example in the lesson and against the materials children most often sort wrongly (NSTA, 'Is It Solid?': powders are called liquids 'because they can be poured', and 'each granule or speck of powder is an individual, tiny piece of solid'). Stone and cloth: no / yes, so solid. Water: yes / no / yes, so liquid. Air: no / no / no, so gas. Sugar, salt, sand or maize meal: can be poured, but question 2 says yes (each grain stays whole), so it does not fit the liquid pattern, which needs no on question 2. No common material in the lesson's world is mis-sorted, and 'baie', not 'alle', makes no claim that the set sorts everything. One edge case: a small drop of water on a waxy surface beads instead of spreading (surface tension; Physics Classroom, 'Surface Tension'). The lesson tests a spill, which does spread (MIT OCW 18.357, Lecture 3: large drops spread to a puddle), so this is not a finding.

items.bewering: Jy kan nie 'n klip of 'n slap lap giet nie. By albei bly elke stuk heel, en hulle is dus vaste stowwe.
items.blok: Hoe jy die drie uitmekaar ken
items.bron: NSTA, 'Is It Solid?' (rock and cloth are both solids). Answers tested literally: holds.

items.bewering: Jy kan water maklik giet, en gemorste water op 'n tafel loop uitmekaar. Daar hou niks dit vas nie, en dit het geen eie vorm nie. Die antwoord op die tweede vraag is dus nee. Sy stil boonste kant lê plat, en dit maak water 'n vloeistof.
items.blok: Hoe jy die drie uitmekaar ken
items.bron: MIT OpenCourseWare 18.357 Interfacial Phenomena, Lecture 3: large drops spread into a puddle (only very small drops stay rounded); Wikipedia, 'Free surface' (a level top at rest). Spilled water spreading out is true for a spill.

items.bewering: Wanneer niks die lug vashou nie, is die antwoord op al drie die vrae nee. Dit maak lug 'n gas.
items.blok: Hoe jy die drie uitmekaar ken
items.bron: Wikipedia, 'State of matter' (a gas has no shape of its own and no free surface; it spreads). Each answer tested: (1) air held by nothing cannot be poured, which is true as worded; (2) it does not stay together; (3) it has no top surface. Boundary noted for a person, not a finding: gases are fluids and a heavy gas CAN be poured (RSC Education and Science in School: carbon dioxide poured from one beaker to another). The sentence is restricted to free air and never says gases cannot be poured, so it does not lead a Grade 4 child to a false conclusion.

items.bron: Wikipedia, 'State of matter' (a solid has a stable, definite shape); NSTA, 'Is It Solid?' (each grain of a powder is a tiny piece of solid, so 'elke stuk' correctly covers sugar and sand). Read on its own: a cloth draping is the known weak point of shape-based definitions (NSTA), but this is CAPS's own property ('vastestowwe behou hul vorm'), and the lesson states outright that a bendy cloth is a solid. Not a false conclusion at Grade 4.

items.bewering: eienskap: Iets wat 'n materiaal doen of is, en waaraan jy dit uitken.
items.blok: eienskap
items.bron: Interglot (Dutch 'eigenschap' = kenmerk, karakteristiek, merkteken) and Vocabulary.com ('eigenschap': something characteristic of an entity); an English dictionary sense of 'property' is a characteristic used to identify a thing. No Afrikaans dictionary entry was found online, but the cognate and the English sense agree. Accurate read on its own.

opsomming: Every checkable claim, every glossary entry read on its own, the three sorting questions tested as a set (including sugar, sand and cloth) and all three activities (stone in a glass and a bowl, squeezing the balloon, the bottle in the bucket) hold at Grade 4 level, so nothing goes back to the writer; there are no superlatives and the few comparisons map correctly; one limit is recorded but is not an error: the lesson says free air cannot be poured, which is true as written, but a heavy gas such as carbon dioxide can be poured, so no later lesson should turn this into 'gases cannot be poured'.
